setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'I know you were speaking a bit with Kim.' No suffix in the title to corroborate, and the call was originally booked for a different closer — 'It looks like you're supposed to speak to Andrew, but... Yeah, I was.'

prospect.name: Vance
prospect.location: Orange County, California, USA (works daily in Los Angeles)
prospect.occupation: Co-owner of an e-commerce clothing brand with his brother; production and fabric sourcing done in LA
prospect.family_status: Runs the business with his brother; nothing else disclosed
prospect.training_background: Gym three to four times a week plus bouldering, inconsistent because of an unpredictable work schedule. Roughly one to two years of training. Bodyweight work — dips and pull-ups. Has been following Trevor on Instagram for about six months and copying kettlebell circuits from social media: halos, helicopters, pullovers, swings, snatches. Has never bought a course or hired a trainer.

signals: Proposed label: the_aspiring_optimizer. He matches the_optimizer on the body and the goal — already lean and training, no medical issues, explicitly wants good to great ('I'd say like I'm fairly healthy. I just want to maintain that and just better myself') — but fails the defining commercial half of that avatar, because price is a real barrier rather than a quality signal. He is 23, does not pay himself a salary, and the money is half his brother's.

Aesthetic and self-improvement driven with no deeper emotional driver available: asked directly whether it was vanity or something else, he said 'Not really, just want to just better myself, really. That's all.'
First-time buyer of any coaching: 'I've never reached out to no one for no guidance' and 'I've never bought a course or paid for a trainer or nothing.'
Self-identified as outside the marketed audience: 'a lot of things I was reading on his page was about like for older people who want to feel young again, you know, not necessarily.'

goals.text: Put on roughly 10-15 lb while staying lean
Get under 10% body fat and add definition to chest, shoulders and arms
Be healthier overall and stay active — named as the number one priority
Transition fully from weightlifting to kettlebells and build functional strength he uses day to day
Have a real plan and structure instead of copying circuits from Instagram
Train time-efficiently around an unpredictable work schedule

pains.text: Training is inconsistent because the work schedule is unfixed — drives an hour and a half to LA whenever production calls
Very slow progress from weightlifting — 'it's very, very slow growth I see in terms of the weight lifting'
Workouts do not feel intense enough even when pushed to failure, unlike kettlebell work
No plan — 'Right now I'm kind of just doing whatever, you know' — piecing circuits together from Instagram
Suspects he is under-eating: 'I think that's maybe something I do struggle with too. Maybe just not eating enough'
Cash is tied up in a business account half-owned by his brother and he takes no set salary

objections.raw_quote: So that's why I wanted to see... See, I did work with Trevor and the team. If there was a way, could just be just like the kettlebell exercises and not nutrition, if that would, you know, have any effect on the price, if it would change less.
objections.rep_response: Deferred it at the time ('we can go into that in few minutes'), then answered it inside the nutrition pillar: the programme does not unbundle. 'We don't really subtract it and then lower the prices. It's just part of the process anyway.' He then reframed by suggesting the prospect might still be eating the wrong whole foods or not enough of them, which the prospect accepted.

objections.raw_quote: But it is a little, you know, expensive.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it cleanly — 'are you saying it's expensive as in I don't have that much money available on hand or like I don't think it's worth that much?' — then ran a worth-it reframe tied to the prospect's stated goals, then opened the financial picture (cash on hand, business versus personal account, whether he pays himself a salary).

objections.raw_quote: So that price is like, like firm as well. Like there's no way to like work around that price or, you know?
objections.rep_response: Did not hold the price. Immediately offered a 3-month option at $4,000, then Primal University at $199/month, then 12-month financing at $650/month with interest.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I think I would definitely have to think about that and maybe get back to you guys. Maybe save a little bit or, you know, because I would like to do a six-month program. I think that would be, like, ideal.
objections.rep_response: Earlier he had probed a similar statement with 'What part?', which worked. This time he accepted it, offered the financing option, and when the prospect repeated 'Definitely just gotta think about it a little more' replied 'Yeah, man.' No next call was booked and no deposit was taken.

offer.payment_plan_terms: 12-month financing on the $6,000 six-month programme at $650/month. Rep: 'it splits the $6K up to a year' and 'Adds a bit of interest, but you can pay it off early. That way you don't have pay the interest.' Twelve payments of $650 is $7,800, i.e. $1,800 of interest on $6,000; neither the total nor the rate was stated.

evidence: Prospect: 'I think we definitely, you know, maybe get back on a call in a little bit. Definitely just gotta think about it a little more.'
Prospect: 'I'm definitely interested in it, but maybe I would have to put a little more thought into that' and 'I would like to do a six-month program. I think that would be, like, ideal.'
Counter-evidence toward lost: he named saving up first — 'Maybe save a little bit' — and most of his money is in a business account he shares 50/50 with his brother
No payment, no payment link, no deposit and no follow-up call actually placed on a calendar, one day after the manager mandated deposits for exactly this situation
Genuine interest is real though: 'it does sound like very, you know, enticing to me'
outcome.next_step: Prospect to think it over and get back in touch; a further call was floated but not scheduled.

notable.note: Two things a manager should see. First, the same unpublished $4,000 three-month tier and the same $650/month financing appeared here as on the David Elder call the previous day, so this is a pattern in this rep's handling of price resistance rather than a one-off improvisation. Second, the rep told a 23-year-old who is 5'10" and 135 lb at a self-reported 12-15% body fat that the programme aims for a body fat drop of 'at least 10%' which 'might put you at five', and called it '100% doable' — a target that is neither realistic nor healthy for this prospect, who also wants to gain weight. No injury or movement-limitation question was asked at any point, despite the prospect being a boulderer about to be moved onto loaded ballistic kettlebell work. Worth crediting the rep on one point: when the prospect's finances looked thin he said 'I don't want you to be like homeless or something' rather than pushing.

quality.notes: Heavy and frequent inversion. Whole passages are attributed to the wrong speaker: at 00:02:24 the prospect's own height and weight are attributed to the rep; at 00:16:11 and 00:17:31 the rep's pitch about the client age range and 'removes a lot of the excuses' is attributed to the prospect; at 00:30:12 the rep's restraint line 'I don't want you to be like homeless or something' and the prospect's 'so that price is firm as well?' are inverted; at 00:34:35 the financing explanation is split across both labels. Role was resolved from content throughout — the rep is whoever is running the process and quoting prices.
